messages:
Ava Holt: Quick sync — dropping a proposed direction for the model catalog compare + filter summary. want quick eyes for a11y and copy before we lock it in.
Marcus Chen: Got it. sending the figma link in a sec. curious about the heatmap density change — does it still convey perf differences at a glance?
Lina Gomez: Figured out a compact heatmap encoding that uses three stop colors + a faint outline for low-sample rows. preserves glanceability in the compact row.
Nicole Park: can you paste a screenshot? color naming will matter for the microcopy. also worried about colorblind contrast.
Lina Gomez: paste: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/compact-compare — the yellow->purple mapping is just a placeholder. outline is 1px #2b2b2b with 20% opacity.
Raj Patel: For a11y: color alone is insufficient. need an assistive summary per row (visually hidden) like "median latency: 73ms; 95th: 210ms; badge: high throughput" — screen readers can read it.
Ava Holt: Good call. UX proposals: 1) add visually-hidden summaries for screen readers; 2) expose keyboard shortcuts to expand a row and reveal performance breakdown; 3) microcopy for badges (e.g., "High throughput" vs "Throughput: high").
Tom Rivera: From an engineering POV, visually-hidden text is fine. keyboard expand should be Enter on focused row and Space on action button. we already have a pattern in the policy list.
Marcus Chen: UI question — should the performance badge be clickable to open the detailed panel, or should clicking the row do it? preference?
Nicole Park: Clickable badge is helpful for targeted drill-ins, but it's a small tap target on mobile. best to make the whole row clickable with a distinct badge action icon as a secondary affordance.
Lina Gomez: I'll prototype that: row click -> detail panel; badge icon button -> anchored tooltip with quick metrics; both expose aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Raj Patel: Make sure the badge has aria-label="Performance: high throughput; click for details" and the tooltip content is announced when focused. Also include a visible focus ring for keyboard nav — 3px contrast-tested.
Ava Holt: Copy tweak: from previous threads we learned users misread "pin version" versus "pin compare". proposal: change CTA to "Pin model version" and tooltip: "Pin this exact variant for compare and rollout". thoughts?
Marcus Chen: +1. Less ambiguous. Also add a small info icon next to the pin with hover copy, and the same text inside the details drawer.
Tom Rivera: backend note: we need to surface whether a pinned version is immutable or auto-updating in the API. will add a field pinned:true/strategy:static|auto. ux should surface that.
Nicole Park: UX should show "Pinned — static" or "Pinned — follows latest patch" in the row subtitle. keep it concise.
Lina Gomez: Accessibility nit: when pin toggle changes state, we must announce it via an ARIA live region: "Version 1.2.3 pinned (static)". otherwise screen readers won't notice the change.
Raj Patel: Also ensure the color contrast of the pin icon meets AA large text if we ever use labels. currently it's 3.8:1 — bump to >=4.5:1 for small icons with no text.
Ava Holt: Performance badge language: avoid ambiguous words like "fast" alone. propose three tiers with defined thresholds: "Low latency (<50ms)", "Moderate (50–150ms)", "High latency (>150ms)". we can show numeric values on hover/tooltip.
Marcus Chen: I like explicit thresholds. Designers: add a small legend in the compare header (toggleable) so users can quickly understand colors and thresholds.
Lina Gomez: Legend won't fit on mobile. propose a collapsible header: default collapsed on small screens, expands on desktop. also provide a persistent "i" icon that opens the legend modal.
Nicole Park: Copy for the legend: short and scannable. example: "Latency tiers — green: <50ms; amber: 50–150ms; red: >150ms. Values shown are median latency across serving region."
Tom Rivera: We'll need to ensure the metric displayed (median vs p95) can be switched in settings — some customers prefer p95. that could affect badge tiers.
Ava Holt: Good point. add a global control (top-right of catalog) to switch the compute metric: median/p95/p50. default to median with tooltip.
Raj Patel: Final a11y pass: keyboard focus order must be logical: filters -> search -> compare rows -> row actions -> detail drawer focus trap. also test with VoiceOver and NVDA.
Marcus Chen: I'll update the Figma with focus states, microcopy, and the legend modal. will ping design-bot when ready for a perf pass.
design-bot: Figma link updated: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/compact-compare — updated states and badge labels. Automated contrast check: 5 items failed (pin icon, tooltip bg, legend text on dark).
Lina Gomez: thanks — I'll iterate on the colors and reduce failures to 0 before the next review.
Ava Holt: Awesome. Next steps: Marcus to update Figma, Lina to fix contrast, Raj to run a quick screen reader script, Tom to add backend flag for pin strategy. aim to reconvene Thursday 11am PT. :calendar: :thumbsup:
Tom Rivera: noted, adding ticket for pinned-strategy toggles.
Nicole Park: I'll draft the final microcopy PR after design updates.
Ava Holt: great work team, thanks!
